keys.prompt: What is the difference between fixed and variable costs?
keys.answer: Fixed costs stay the same no matter how much you sell, like a sign. Variable costs go up with every sale, like cups.

cards.title: Did your stand make money?
cards.text: Say you sold $30 of lemonade on Saturday. Did you make $30? Not so fast. What did you have to buy to make it?

cards.question: Your sign and pitcher cost $12. Each cup sells for $1 and costs 40 cents to make. How many cups do you need to sell to stop losing money?
cards.reveal: 20 cups. Each cup gives you 60 cents toward your $12, and 20 times 60 cents is $12. Every cup after that is profit!

cards.title: Money in, money out
cards.text: Revenue is all the money that comes in from selling. Costs are all the money you spend to make and sell your product. Profit is what is left: revenue minus costs.
cards.example: If you sold $30 and spent $18, your profit is $12.

cards.title: Two kinds of costs
cards.text: Some costs stay the same no matter how much you sell, like a sign or a pitcher. These are fixed costs. Other costs go up with every cup you sell, like lemons and cups. These are variable costs.

why.q: Why are paper cups a variable cost, but a pitcher is not?
why.a: You need one more cup for every sale. You buy a pitcher once, no matter how much you sell.

cards.title: The break-even point
cards.text: Break-even is when the money coming in equals all your costs. You have not lost money, and you have not made any yet. Every sale after that is profit.
cards.example: Say your sign and pitcher cost $12. Each cup sells for $1 and costs 40 cents to make. Each cup gives you 60 cents toward your $12. You need 20 cups to break even.

examples_by_interest.art: Say you sell bookmarks you paint. Paint and brushes cost $12 once. Each bookmark sells for $1, and its paper costs 40 cents. Each sale gives 60 cents toward your $12, so you need 20 to break even.
examples_by_interest.soccer: Say your soccer team sells water at a game. The cooler costs $12. Each bottle sells for $1 and costs 40 cents. Each bottle gives 60 cents toward the cooler, so you need 20 to break even.

cards.title: Plan for surprises
cards.text: A U.S. government office that helps small businesses has a tip. When you plan, add about 10% extra to your costs. Surprises happen, like spilled lemonade!

cards.question: If you raise your price from $1 to $2 a cup, you need fewer cups to break even. But what else might change?
nudges: What would you do to make your lemonade worth $2?
